pleistocene.summary: The epoch of repeated glacial cycles, during which ice sheets advanced and retreated more than twenty times and the genus Homo spread across the globe.

homo-sapiens.summary: Anatomically modern humans appear in Africa and subsequently disperse across every continent.
homo-sapiens.note: The Jebel Irhoud fossils push anatomically modern traits back to about 315 ka; fully modern morphology is usually placed nearer 200 ka.

last-glacial-period.summary: The most recent ice age, when ice sheets covered much of North America and northern Eurasia and sea level fell by about 125 metres.

toba-eruption.summary: A supervolcanic eruption in Sumatra, the largest of the Quaternary, followed by a volcanic winter of disputed severity.

aboriginal-australia.summary: Humans crossed Wallacea to reach Sahul, beginning the longest continuous cultural tradition known.

last-glacial-maximum.summary: The peak of the last ice age, when continental ice sheets reached their greatest extent and Beringia linked Asia to the Americas.
